activities.anchor: is the response of believers to what they hold sacred
activities.caption: file each act of worship by its setting
activities.name: wsWorshipSort

config.prompt: Two settings, one heartbeat — file each act:

items.label: a Muslim man expected at the Friday midday prayer
certain Jewish prayers requiring a quorum of ten adults — the minyan
a congregation gathering to transmit tradition to children
the personal prayer at a bedside
the quiet reading of scripture alone
the rosary counted on a bus

config.why: The two feed each other — the communal service teaches the words, and the private prayer uses them.

activities.anchor: worship means singing songs in a special building
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a worship briefing
activities.name: wsSingingSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on what worship is, is wrong — click it:
lines: Prayer, scripture reading, ritual meals, silence and pilgrimage are all worship.
None of them needs a building — a Muslim may pray on any clean ground.
A Jewish family performs the Shabbat table ritual at home.
Worship requires a special building, and singing is the definition of it.
config.correction: Worship is any reverent response to the sacred, public or private, anywhere — the building is a container the tradition builds for it, not the thing itself.
config.why: Singing is one act among many — the slice most visible on screen, which is why the misconception sticks.

activities.name: wsArtefactMatch

config.prompt: Each object does doctrinal work — pair them:

pairs.right: the sacrifice emphasised — common in Catholic and Anglican worship
pointing to the resurrection — many Protestant churches
windows to the holy — honoured but not worshipped

config.why: None of this is decoration by accident — the furniture list of each tradition is really its priorities made visible.

activities.caption: true or false — the ministry roster
activities.name: wsMinistryJudge

statements.s: A priest (Catholic, Orthodox) can celebrate the Eucharist and hears confession.
statements.why: The vicar or rector is the Anglican incumbent of a parish.

statements.s: Pastor and minister stress preaching and care over sacrament — the words mean shepherd and servant.
statements.why: The Protestant vocabulary signals what the role is for.

statements.s: Bishops oversee many churches in a district — a diocese; deacons stand for service and assistance.
statements.why: Around them, lay people read lessons, serve at the altar or lead children's work.

statements.s: All Christian traditions ordain only celibate men.
statements.why: Many Pentecostal and Baptist churches ordain whoever the congregation recognises as gifted, including women — the leader is a function, not a caste.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the absolution distinction
activities.name: wsAbsolutionCloze

config.text: Catholic teaching is more precise: the priest acts %%0%% — as the visible instrument of God's forgiveness — and absolution belongs to %%1%%; the priest is the means, not the source.
config.hint: The Latin phrase for 'in the person of Christ' — and to whom absolution ultimately belongs.

config.why: Worship here is a whole-body sequence, shoulder to shoulder in rows — which is why the hall is deliberately empty: no seats, no images, no altar.

activities.anchor: Jewish worship happens as much at home
activities.caption: drag the divider — where the reading stands
activities.name: wsBimahCompare

config.prompt: Two ways a sacred text could meet a congregation — drag the divider.

before.label: Performed at the congregation
before.text: A reading done from the far front — an audience receiving a performance.

after.label: Read from the middle
after.text: The bimah, a raised platform at the centre: the word of God is read from the middle of the community, not performed at it from the front.

config.why: Around the ark (aron kodesh) holding the Torah scrolls and the ever-burning ner tamid, the synagogue's furniture states its priorities — the scroll read from within the community.

activities.anchor: each garment is a worn reminder
activities.caption: pair each garment with what it reminds
activities.name: wsDressMatch

config.prompt: Ritual dress — pair each garment with its reminder:

pairs.right: covers the head in acknowledgment that God is above
knotted fringes commanded in the Torah as a physical prompt to keep the commandments
two small leather boxes with scripture, strapped to the arm near the heart and the forehead
the prayer shawl whose corners carry the fringes

config.why: Each garment is commandment worn on the body — and dress varies by community: Orthodox seating and Hebrew-only prayer, Reform mixed seating and women rabbis; both are 'synagogues'.
